November 18, 2026

US strikes missile site on Iran's Qeshm Island

tags: war, politics, markets
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy, @oafnation_actual

The US military carried out what it described as precision defensive strikes on Qeshm Island in Iran, targeting a missile launch site in retaliation for Iranian attacks on US personnel and assets, according to a US military official cited by Reuters. Qeshm is the largest island in the Persian Gulf, lies at the mouth of the Strait of Hormuz where roughly 17 million barrels of crude pass daily, and is home to about 150,000 people as well as underground missile and naval facilities. Iranian officials said nothing critical was hit and that no infrastructure was damaged; CENTCOM said it had no updates. A third US aircraft carrier, the Roosevelt, is moving to the region, and analysts expect pressure on oil and diesel prices.

Bahrain and Kuwait intercept Iranian aerial attacks

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Bahrain intercepted new Iranian aerial attacks on Wednesday and Kuwait engaged hostile drones, according to Reuters. Bahrain issued two threat alerts before giving the all-clear, and Kuwait said explosions heard in the country were interceptions. The wave came a day after exchanges of US and Iranian strikes, including Iranian drones fired at a US radar system in Bahrain.

Trump holds trilateral summit with Putin and Xi, pledges to rein in the ICC

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump met Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in China in what was described as the first trilateral meeting between the three countries, calling both leaders his friends. The three signed a declaration covering four areas: reforming the United Nations, reining in the International Criminal Court, petroleum exports and nuclear weapons. Trump said he would work to shield Putin and Xi from ICC war crimes prosecution, even though Putin is subject to an active arrest warrant. Reporters travelling with the delegation said their phones were confiscated as the group left China.

Congress sends preservation letters to Trump family and top officials

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Representative Robert Garcia sent document preservation letters to six people, including Jared Kushner, Donald Trump Jr., Eric Trump, JD Vance, Susie Wiles and Stephen Miller. The letters notify the recipients that they will be subject to three investigations: the handling of the Epstein files, Trump family businesses, and matters relating to ICE. The move came despite threats from the administration to prosecute those pursuing the inquiries.

Army to detonate 68 barrels of lead azide in Iowa as evacuations and school closures widen

tags: health, environment, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

The US Army will hold two controlled detonations Friday at its Middletown, Iowa ammunition plant to destroy about 68 barrels of degraded, crystallized lead azide deemed too unstable to move. Residents near the plant have been asked to evacuate from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. over possible window damage, schools in Burlington, New London and Danville will close, and Davenport schools will keep students indoors because of a possible plume of toxic lead dust. University of Iowa researchers and residents have raised concerns about contamination reaching soil, waterways including the Mississippi River, and wildlife, with children under six considered most vulnerable. Illinois Governor J.B. Pritzker said the Department of Defense is responsible for preventing harm and is pressing for answers, while reporting indicates Iowa leaders were not told well in advance despite the Army knowing since April.

NSA classified network outage stretches into a third day

tags: surveillance, tech, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews, @ericmoutsos

NSA Net, the National Security Agency's internal network for exchanging and storing classified material, went down Tuesday and disruptions have continued for three days. Two sources traced the outage to routine software updates and US officials said they had seen no evidence of a cyberattack; the agency staggered arrival times for non-emergency staff at Fort Meade under a schedule known as Code Gray. CNN later reported the disruption also hit a critical Georgia facility supporting signals intelligence and cybersecurity operations focused on the Middle East, after the agency had initially described the problem as temporary degradation. The European Commission was also reported to have been hit by a cyberattack, though no link between the incidents has been established.

Homeland Security says Iran-linked hackers have targeted US infrastructure for months

tags: tech, defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told Congress in written testimony for a worldwide threats hearing that hackers linked to Iran have been targeting US critical infrastructure for months. He said the attacks have hit transportation, healthcare, water, energy and financial services. Mullin said the recent wave of technology outages was not linked to those attacks.

House Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @groundnews

House Democrats chose Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York as their candidate for speaker by a vote of 251 to 11, with two members not voting, in a closed-door caucus meeting. Democrats are projected to hold at least 257 seats after the midterms, giving Jeffries a path to the gavel when the full House votes in January. If elected he would be the first Black speaker of the House. The nomination followed a dispute within the caucus over whether to replace its leaders.

Peltola flips Alaska Senate seat, giving Democrats a 56-44 majority

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews, @carolinegleich

Democrat Mary Peltola defeated Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska, the last Senate race of the 2026 midterms to be called, making it the ninth Democratic flip this cycle and the party's largest gain since 1958. Peltola, who is Yup'ik, will be the first Alaska Native elected to the Senate and joins Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota as the first Native women to serve there. The count took two weeks because Alaska allows mailed absentee ballots up to ten days to arrive; projections show Peltola cleared 50%, avoiding a ranked-choice tally. The Justice Department sued to block certification over a second candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., a judge dismissed the suit, and the department has appealed and confirmed a criminal investigation, though counts show Peltola outpolled both Sullivans combined.

Kushner failed to disclose $32 million stake in defense contractor

tags: politics, legal, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

The Atlantic reported that Jared Kushner did not publicly disclose a $32 million stake, held through his firm Affinity Partners, in an American defense contractor that profits from conflicts he has been mediating. SEC filings show the holding was disclosed on November 5, two days after the midterm elections, although it was due to be reported in August.

Timeline questions Trump's decisions on Nvidia chip sales to China

tags: tech, politics, markets
sources: @carolinegleich

A detailed account of US AI export policy notes that Trump cancelled the rule requiring AI companies to share safety test results on his first day back in office, banned Nvidia's H20 chip sales to China in April 2025, then dropped the ban in July 2025 after meeting Nvidia's CEO, with the government taking 15% of sales, and approved the stronger H200 in December 2025 with a 25% cut. Reports say Trump was warned in fall 2025 and again by his Secretary of State in May 2026 that Nvidia's CEO was close to a woman US intelligence believes is a Chinese spy, and took him to Beijing regardless. Nvidia gave $25 million toward the White House ballroom in October 2025, and Trump reportedly held between $13 million and $62 million in Nvidia stock in August 2026. Roughly $12 billion in top Nvidia chips were reportedly lined up for Chinese buyers through Megaspeed, a company run by the alleged spy, and a government investigation into it reportedly stalled; calls are being made for public congressional hearings under oath.

Jensen Huang says he would return as Nvidia CEO

tags: tech, markets
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

Former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said he would be honoured to return to lead the chipmaker, a week after resigning amid reports of an affair with a woman allegedly linked to Chinese intelligence and affairs with employees. Huang acknowledged his conduct, said he deeply regretted creating problems for the board, and committed to cooperating with an independent investigation by law firm Wachtell Lipton into whether his conduct exposed company secrets or created national security risks. Sources told CNBC the board is not considering reinstating him, while more than 180,000 people have signed a petition supporting his return and Trump said he was open to it.

Senate permitting bill BAAJA draws objections over tribal consultation and data center power

tags: climate, politics, tech
sources: @carolinegleich

The Senate is moving toward passing BAAJA, a permitting bill that would fast-track gas pipelines, gas power plants and nuclear projects, many of them intended to supply electricity to data centers. Critics say Title III would weaken the legal requirement that tribes be consulted before federal projects harm sacred sites, pointing to fights over Bears Ears, Chaco Canyon and Oak Flat, and note that tribal nations had no real role in drafting it. An amendment from Senator Schiff would strike Title III while leaving the rest of the bill intact. Concerns have also been raised about the bill's implications for clean water, climate and public lands, alongside claims that posts opposing it are being throttled on Meta platforms.

Trump nominee for government watchdog faces rushed confirmation

tags: politics, legal
sources: @carolinegleich

Trump has nominated Eric Ueland, a senior official at the White House budget office, to lead the Government Accountability Office, the congressional watchdog that tracks federal spending and has already ruled that some of the administration's spending moves broke the law. Critics say Ueland helped run the same programs he would be judging, and that the post carries a 15-year term running to 2041 from which no president can remove him. The law provides for a bipartisan group of House and Senate leaders to vet candidates first, a process that took more than a year last time; this time the group never met and lawmakers were given 24 hours to submit names. The hearing was scheduled for the following morning, with Republicans seeking to confirm him before Democrats take the Senate in January.

Incoming Texas attorney general to drop abortion enforcement cases

tags: politics, legal, health
sources: @aaronparnas

Nathan Johnson, the Democrat elected to replace Ken Paxton as Texas attorney general, told the Houston Chronicle he will end Republican-led efforts to restrict abortion in the state. He said he will drop lawsuits Paxton filed against medical providers who sent abortion medication into Texas and will respect the shield laws of other states.

US joins Russia in opposing UN resolution on violence against women

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

The United States was among seven countries that voted against or abstained on a United Nations draft resolution aimed at intensifying global efforts to prevent and eliminate all forms of violence against women and girls. The others were Somalia, Russia, Burkina Faso, Belarus, Argentina and Cameroon. The measure passed with 175 votes in favour, one against and six abstentions.

US loses measles elimination status after 26 years

tags: health, politics
sources: @groundnews

The Pan American Health Organization announced that the United States has lost its measles elimination status for the first time in 26 years, following more than 7,700 reported infections and over 10 deaths since the start of 2025. A country loses the designation after 12 consecutive months of domestic transmission, a threshold the US reached in January, and cases have more than doubled last year's total. PAHO also revoked the elimination status of Mexico and Bolivia. Public health officials called for a nationwide vaccination campaign, but CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the decision would not change the federal response.

Judge strikes down four-year cap on foreign student stays

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @groundnews

US District Judge F. Dennis Saylor struck down a Department of Homeland Security rule that capped foreign students' stays in the country at four years, calling it arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion and not in accordance with law. The July rule required students to seek an extension if they needed more time to finish their degrees, replacing a policy that let them stay while enrolled and in good standing. Education advocacy groups had challenged the rule, arguing it would deter students from coming to the United States, and the department's general counsel criticized the ruling.

Norway's Equinor says it is fighting an ongoing cyberattack

tags: tech, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

Equinor, the Norwegian state-majority-owned energy company, said publicly that it detected and is fighting an ongoing cyberattack and has informed authorities, according to a statement cited by Reuters. The company said it is mobilizing resources to neutralize the attack and regain full integrity, and has so far seen no data stolen and no impact on operations or output. Equinor is one of the largest natural gas suppliers to Europe. Who carried out the attack and how access was gained are not known.

Senators warn AI cyber threats are outpacing US defenses

tags: tech, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Senators Maria Cantwell and Mike Rounds urged immediate White House action to protect critical infrastructure, banks and widely used software from AI-enabled cyber threats, according to Reuters. They called for defensive AI tools and stronger standards governing autonomous agents.

Ukrainian strikes destroy major sections of the Kerch bridge

tags: war, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

The Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia has been struck by Ukraine over multiple days, and major parts of the structure are now destroyed. The bridge has been a signature project for Vladimir Putin since Russia's annexation of Crimea.

Ukraine plans to double drone supply and triple long-range strikes

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhenii Khmara said the country plans to double its drone supplies and more than triple long-range strikes next year, according to Military Times. Britain will send more than 1,000 long-range drones in a $342 million package. Kyiv is proceeding despite Pentagon criticism of deep strikes inside Russia.

House Republicans use Ukraine aid as leverage over Pentagon oversight

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Top House Republicans are using Ukraine provisions in the annual defense bill as a bargaining chip to pressure Democrats into dropping stronger oversight of Defense Secretary Hegseth and President Trump, according to NBC News. Senator Jack Reed said a bill without the Ukraine aid would be dead on arrival.

Navy secretary nominee pressed on sailor malnutrition and war costs

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

At his confirmation hearing, Hung Cao, Trump's nominee for Navy secretary, disputed reports that sailors had lost 45 pounds, comparing it to his children saying there is nothing to eat in the refrigerator. Senator Mark Kelly, a former carrier pilot, rejected that characterization and noted the Secretary of Defense had dismissed the issue when it was raised. Senator Elissa Slotkin pressed Cao on the cost of the ongoing war and on the administration's refusal to brief Congress, noting the budget was written before the conflict began and that the Defense Secretary has held about two press conferences in six months. Cao said the department would do its best to provide the information.

Trump nominates Gen. Chris LaNeve as Army chief of staff

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Trump has nominated General Chris LaNeve to be the Army's chief of staff. LaNeve has served as acting chief since April, after General Randy George was fired for refusing to remove Black and female officers from the Army's one-star promotion list. Before that, LaNeve gained internal support for helping end an investigation into two Army Apache helicopters that flew low over Kid Rock's property. Confirmation will require Republican support, and Senator Joni Ernst has previously expressed hesitation about his leadership.

Thirty Marines discharged within two years of reporting sexual assault

tags: defence, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

An investigation by The War Horse, reported via Military Times, found that over five years 30 Marines were administratively discharged within two years of reporting a sexual assault. The Marine Corps says it strictly enforces protections against retaliation. Advocates say survivors still fear that reporting will cost them their careers.

Pentagon watchdog flags fraud and failed audit as top challenges

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Defense Department inspector general listed eliminating fraud and achieving a clean audit among seven top management challenges, according to Military Times. The report said the Pentagon continues to fund contractors that fail to deliver or that run years behind schedule.

Justice Department charges 15 in veterans benefits fraud crackdown

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Justice Department said its first coordinated surge against VA benefits fraud brought charges involving more than $3.4 million in intended losses. Pleas, verdicts and sentencings in related cases topped $19 million in intended losses. The effort began September 1 with the Department of Veterans Affairs and its inspector general.

Saudi Arabia expects Yemen war to run into 2027

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Saudi Arabia is preparing for its war against Yemen's Houthis to stretch well into 2027, according to Reuters. Two Western officials briefed by Saudi officials said Riyadh foresees up to six more months of fighting before any negotiations. The Houthis have advanced toward Aden in recent days.

Thousands march in Haiti to thank Bukele for sending troops

tags: politics, war
sources: @groundnews

Thousands demonstrated in Port-au-Prince and elsewhere in Haiti to thank Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele for deploying troops against gangs. Bukele sent about 2,500 soldiers in October after an attack left four Salvadoran aviation technicians missing, and Salvadoran officials said the troops would leave once the technicians are found. Gangs hold an estimated 70% of the capital and more than 20,000 people have died in the violence over five years. The International Crisis Group said Haiti lacks a plan to curb gang violence once foreign forces leave.

Claim puts Gaza death toll far above official counts

tags: war, politics
sources: @ericmoutsos

An account circulating argues that the true death toll in Gaza is around 600,000, far above the roughly quarter-million previously estimated, on the grounds that official tallies count only bodies that reach hospitals or funerals and exclude those buried under rubble. The claim holds that about half the dead are older men, women and children, many killed by 2,000-pound bombs supplied by the United States. It also references a pending US transfer of between 40,000 and 60,000 additional weapons to Israel. The figures are assertions rather than confirmed counts.

Trump privately venting about Vance and Paxton

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

According to the New York Times, Trump has been privately venting about JD Vance for publicly breaking with him on the war in Iran and saying the war was why Republicans lost. The Daily Mail reported he has also complained about Ken Paxton, his former endorsed candidate in Texas who lost to James Talarico, attributing the defeat to Paxton's appearance. Reporting indicates Vance's standing has weakened while Secretary of State Rubio's has risen.

Musk says he is not MAGA and calls his midterm spending foolish

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Speaking at the DealBook summit, Elon Musk said he is not MAGA, having previously described himself as dark MAGA, and called himself a fool for spending hundreds of millions of dollars on the midterm elections. He described an incoming Democratic governor as a moderate and said they would work well together, adding that he wants to work with Democrats.

Midterms produce record number of women in state legislatures

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews

The midterm elections will bring a record 2,559 or more women to state legislatures, according to Rutgers University's Center for American Women and Politics, up from the previous high of 2,488 seats. With some races undecided, women are set to hold about 35% of legislative seats nationwide, with the increase driven by Democratic gains; the center counted at least 675 Republican women, down from 867. Women will make up half or more of lawmakers in a record six states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Delaware, Nevada and New Mexico.

Anthropic reaches $2 trillion valuation in Nasdaq debut

tags: markets, tech
sources: @groundnews

Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq Thursday at a $2 trillion valuation, becoming the first frontier AI developer to list its shares and eclipsing SpaceX's June debut. The stock opened at $111.50, 34% above its $83 IPO price, and the company raised more than $107 billion, including $26 billion from a private placement backed by Microsoft, Nvidia and Google, selling 980 million shares. Demand held up during a selloff in technology stocks as investors questioned whether AI spending would pay off. The company has close to $900 billion in commitments for computing capacity with providers including Amazon and Google.

Firefighters respond to fire at CIA headquarters

tags: politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Firefighters were reported responding to a fire at CIA headquarters in Langley, Virginia, according to local reports. No further details on the cause or extent were given.
